title: WOMEN'S BASKETBALL | Sam Purcell Media Session - 11/16/26
text: First and foremost, glad to be back home. Um super proud of my team for a crazy travel weekend and blessed the good Lord had us with we went commercial to Buffalo and FAA obviously shut down right when we landed and didn't know if we would return home and found a way to win a tough game with an unbelievable atmosphere up in Buffalo. I want to give another thank you to them um for allowing us to come up there and most importantly bringing Madison back home, but just again thanking good Lord that was able to return the team safe. Uh Everett our bus driver I want to give him a shout out. We had flew to Atlanta and then our flight got canceled back so he drove all the way to Atlanta, picked us up and we got home at 3:00 in the morning. I'm sure all my kids slept till 3:00 p.m. yesterday and they better be in class right now as we speak and then we need to bounce back and have one great day of practice and then one of my favorite games of the year um outside of opening of SEC play and the Christmas game this is right up there in the kids game and thinking we're going to have 7,000 young kids. Everybody bring your earmuffs, right? Media you guys are going to be in trouble. You know how loud that game is and what's always fun is they're not only going to cheer for us, they're also cheer for Alabama State, right? So the mascot has their work cut out and making sure the energy's favoring Mississippi State um and I know they'll do a great job, but then it just whatever tickets we have left let's let's let's make it a sell out tomorrow for an unbelievable opportunity for women's basketball. >> Yeah, with Maddie's homecoming over the weekend just how do you think she enjoyed [clears throat and cough] that whole experience not even just the game, but just all the other activities you were able to do and see Buffalo? >> Yeah, it's you know I talked to her before we went. I I think she's probably now that she's had time to reflect over the last 24 hours. Um you know anytime you're young you don't understand the magnitude uh even at the age of you know 18 to 24 year old or 23 old these college kids are of what kind of true impact you can make on the young generation. Um, and I think one it was cool for her to see the warm welcome she received going back home, uh, which was really cool. There were several several uh, fans. It was one of their most high attended games and again that's why I shout out uh, Buffalo Women's Basketball for allowing us to come back. It was a two for one. It was one and it was cool for to allow one of theirs to be honored. But then also they want to that she's doing a really good job trying to fight for their program and try to win fans over. So it was a win win, but just the crowd that was able to attend that game, the t-shirts and then again for us in this program um, it's more than just basketball. Um, you know, we were able to go to the Boys and Girls Club um, which really gave me goosebumps and I think our our behind the scenes crew did a great job for you know, for you all to see the photos and the videos of the little kids um, was really again what this program is about. It's bigger than basketball and I think she accomplished a lot of that um, you know, and and I know I'm kind of speaking long on it because it was really cool. Um, but I told her you know, there's three things in life um, you know, for these young kids to understand is one uh, to dream big cuz Madison Francis dreamed as big as anybody um, and had the courage to move away from home and look what she did her freshman year. The second one she did it through hard work um, and then number three is uh, never forgetting where you're from. And so that's part of my commitment to these young ladies when given the opportunity. If we can play a game close back to home, I'm always going to do it cuz I appreciate them sacrificing leaving from home to come here. So that's kind of the long-winded one, Sam. I don't know if you wanted all that, but I gave it to you this morning. >> Jay. >> Sort of building off that, but you had like the most Madison Francis E box score of her season this year too. Just going to talk about how she played and and just you know, what she looked like >> Yeah, so again I I can't say enough about my team and their toughness. Uh, you know, just to give you a little um, backstory, you know, the young ladies woke up on I'm going to get my day straight here, Friday, right? At 3:00 a.m. in the morning. We catch a 6:00 a.m. flight out of here at GTR, landing at Atlanta, get to Buffalo. I think we landed like what, 1:30 2:00. FA, you know, FAA, you know, reports at 3:30 that all shutdowns going on. So then you can imagine just like what's going on? Like we're away from home, you know, and there's just like anybody, human nature, it's anxiety arises. And then you just try to get them in a good mindset that hey, listen, we're going to go to Niagara Falls, right? Let's go enjoy life. Let's go do some other cool things, which again was just breathtaking. It was huge for me for the connectivity of this team. And then, you know, you try to get them rest. We lose an hour going East Coast and then we, you know, agreed to do an early morning game at 12:00 and to think we start off slow. I know there's going to probably be a lot of the questions, but I couldn't be more happy, right? My team was awake. They were tough. They found a way. We knew where they get their best punch and by the end of four quarters, it was really good for our team and it was always also really good for Madison. And then just like I'm trying to tell them right now, I'm actually glad we lost the first quarter. I am, right? We We've been up every game. I need adversity. And I've talked about this. I only got three kids on the team that are returning. So let's find out who we got. Let's see how you handle things. Okay, things didn't go well. What's up? We got to correct it and fix it. And I thought not only her but the rest of her teammates did a great job of that this weekend. >> Reese is your point guard, but how do you want her to balance looking for her own shot versus looking to pass the ball to her teammate? >> Yeah, outstanding question. Okay, because the stats have showed she's 27 assists already in four games. Like good grief, right? Like, you know, and I know I can speak for her teammates. It's it's fun to play with her. She just has a vision. I mean, there's several times she could have took some bad shots, but there was one that she had a deep pick and roll I'll never forget. It was in front of our bench, I think the third quarter with her in favor and she had like a pull up from me to you and she made that dump pass. It's just who the kid is. But I told her in these certain games, and we've pointed out in film and I challenged her teammates and one thing you all are going to consistently hear from me right now is do I love this team? You better believe it. But we have to be direct with each other for us to win the big games that we need to win. Um and one of that goes with Reese. When Reese always kicks it out to everybody else, she's very direct and she's my surgeon to let you know make that shot. But to your question, they have to do that for her. So when they drive and they kick it to her, uh we've shown it on film several times, I need you to shoot that shot. And I thought it was great she did in transition uh in the first half. She made a trail three right there at the top of the key and I just told her, okay, that's the one we need. Keep being that when those opportunities present itself. >> Do you have an update on Kali after her injury? >> Yeah, no no update today. >> Just, you know, you mentioned that this is one of your favorite games of the year tomorrow. Just talk about more why you why you love this game so much. >> Yeah, well first of all, I'm a father of three three kids myself. Um and then it's kind of like we talked about with Chautau, where we were able to sell that out. Again, shout out to Pearl River and Chief Ben for partnering up with us this year to do a really cool event. Um and again, I try to help educate everybody. The women's game's different from the men's. Are we both playing basketball? You better believe it. But we have to fight for a different space. And I'm not speaking on emotions, I'm speaking on facts. Right? So for us, our audience is different. And so our ticket prices are different, right? And there's nothing wrong with that, right? We're you know, the women's game's going into a great spot. The WNBA couldn't be in a better spot right now with, you know, the sold out. Like I love where our game's growing. But for us, and this is where I try to educate my young women is there's a kid who's going to get on a school bus whose family can't afford to take you to a game at all, right? And and and I can guarantee my paycheck or my house on this and that this is the only time they get the chance to watch basketball at the highest stage. And they're going to have the most fun ever because there's going to be 8,000 people who are my age and little kids running around together providing hopefully, you know, we get 67 on the board again. 67 right? That's their thing. Uh that this place goes nuts. Um, but they also leave out of there mad, and I only have a great time. Did I eat popcorn? But you know what? That young lady inspired me. And now I'm going to go home and get in my driveway, and I'm going to play basketball. And then you never know where that's going to take you. Again, I talked about bringing Madison Francis back home and dreaming big. That kid now goes to bed dreaming about the experience they they had because of what a school opportunity provide. And that's why that that game gives me goosebumps, and that's why like you've seen in the past, we'll sign autographs as long as those buses are here because we want to touch every single one of those kids and let them know you could be the next Mississippi State Bulldog here in the future. >> Uh, coach, Macy Pfeifer had eight points and 10 rebounds. Uh, what did you see from her performance off the bench? >> Wow. Can I I can't say enough about her again. Just she's doing exactly what I asked in the recruiting process. Obviously, this is a young lady at MTSU that scored I think like 15 points a game, 14 or 15. Um, and I asked her I need this role Your role's going to be different this first year. Uh, I need you to be the glue for our team. And that's what she was. In a slow start, she came in and gave huge minutes. I thought the play of the game was for me again in the first half. I can see it in my head. We ran one of our little sweet plays on the baseline, which is for her to score. She knew where Callie Smallwood was, opposite, caught the ball. You saw this. And through a direct skip pass faster than I've ever seen that was on rhythm and was just a dagger three that I was like, holy smokes. What an IQ play. And that's where to your points, I know you gave me the box score, but that's what I love about that kid, and that's what I'm trying to show my team. I have a lot of those players who are making those plays. Do not get caught up, and you heard me say this last time. And I'm big I'm on one today, Sam. Sorry. I'm long-winded. All right? Is is I want the same. I don't want more right now. Same is okay. If you're giving me the same every day, then it's consistency. And Macy Pfeifer gives me consistency every day with her smile, her energy, her work ethic, her willing to be the ultimate team player, her making the high IQ plays that sometimes don't go into the box score, but most importantly helped win for this team. And and I really appreciate that kid, and I'm excited to see her get off to a great start. >> If Cali does have to miss some time, who would be some of the players you would need to count on to to step up in her role? >> Yeah, so we've talked about this. Aris, uh last game, right? Obviously, will be one huge. She did it two games ago. Only reason she didn't have back-to-back games is I just got to help her with foul trouble. Uh you know, me and her are going to have a talk again today where she plays so hard, but in the women's game here right now it's being called a certain way, so we got to adapt. We got to pivot and we got to adjust. And I know she will. I'll show her on film. Sometimes you just need four games to realize, okay, coach is right, right? Cuz this again is not emotion, it's facts. Um because I sat her down and she didn't realize she had three fouls in the Buffalo game and I said, okay, that's where I'm trying to help you. That's where I'll be a better coach to let you know, hey, you got two. You got one. So now you got to make those adjustments because she's so special for us with her energy and athleticism. Uh and then Ludo, obviously, and then Macy. Macy played some three the other day. Uh you know, she's again my glue piece where she's got guard tendencies. She can play the post, so it gives me a lot of options for people to step up and I I expect those young ladies to definitely do that. >> I know it's a short turnaround, but what do you want to what have you seen from Alabama State and what do you want to see from your team tomorrow? >> Yeah, so you know, again, ton of respect. We've played them every year. I appreciate them uh agreeing to come here, especially for an early game for them, right? Um you know, we know we're going to get their best. Um I know the season hasn't started the way they want. They won and three. Um but you saw what they did. Uh and I appreciate her mindset um as a coach. This is the same program who came in here last year with a similar record, but if you looked at what they did in conference, they made it to the championship. That's why they play these games. They want to play the toughest tough so then when they get in their conference, they can make a run like no other and hopefully make the NCAA tournament. So again, this is a program that knows how to win. She's been there 13 seasons. Um we need to come in with a lot of respect. Uh we and then what I want to see from my team again is the message and I said, I'm really on one right now. I don't want more, more, more. I want the same. I want the same mindset that I know we had a long travel day, ladies, but today's practice. I need you to crush practice. I need us to connect. I need to be direct. I need us to work on what we're not good at right now and continue to you know, keep that identity about what we are and then respect the game. To think that you're going to have 7,000 kids here tomorrow, I need you to play with a lot of gratitude cuz that's what again life can take you go way fast, but you got to wake up and thank the good Lord that you know what? I got a chance to put that Mississippi State jersey on. I get to lace those shoes up, but most importantly, I got a chance to play in front of 7,000 kids that are going to think I'm an absolute rock star. So baby, have fun and let's go for four quarters. >> All right, thanks everybody. >> Thank you all. Have a great day.
